description:
## Empirical anchor

2026-05-13 surfaced by project-tier PLINY during ariadne--8fd.12 (factory-demo seeder + run). Phase 6 corpus build authored gap tickets (T-0390/T-0391/T-0392/T-0393) intended to block the master epic (T-0001) — structurally a descendant-blocks-ancestor relationship (gaps are children of the investigation; the gaps' presence-or-absence is what the master-epic synthesizes).

**bw 0.13.0 rejects these edges.** From the 0.13.0 release notes: 'Reject child-blocks-ancestor dependencies — bw dep add now rejects edges where a descendant blocks one of its own ancestors (in addition to the existing cycle check). A descendant blocking its ancestor is a logical contradiction — the ancestor can never become unblocked.'

This is logically correct for ticket-tracker semantics ('the ancestor can never become unblocked' = stuck-forever, bad). But it's structurally incomplete for hypergraph/absence-evidence use cases where:
- The 'ancestor' is a master investigation/epic ticket
- The 'descendants' are evidence nodes (including absence-evidence / gap tickets)
- The block edge represents 'this investigation cannot conclude without addressing this evidence/gap'
- The 'never becomes unblocked' is the POINT — open gap = open investigation = correct demo behavior

The factory-demo Q4 query (hypergraph gap-traversal) depends on these edges being visible. The seeder logged the rejection + persisted the edges in the manifest only (.seed_state.json + CORPUS_MANIFEST.jsonl), not in bw's dependency graph.

## Substrate touch-point

**operating-disciplines.md §16** (bw-fit matrix + bw/Ariadne/hypergraph layered-architecture, landed Arc 23 via stoa--vmc) currently has two columns: 'bw is the right choice' / 'NOT bw — use direct Postgres, beads-on-Dolt, or another DB engine'.

Add a third row class to the matrix: **'bw + manifest-only relationship class'** — for use cases where bw is the right write-side substrate for the bulk of relationships, BUT specific relationship classes (descendant→ancestor blocks, particular hypergraph edges) cannot be represented in bw's dependency model and must live in the projection layer (Ariadne / hypergraph / a sidecar manifest) only.

Examples to include:
- Gap-tracking in investigative workflows (factory-manager demo Q4)
- Absence-evidence in hypergraph traversal
- Any 'open-forever-by-design' edge that bw correctly rejects as stuck-forever

## Discipline rule

When designing a corpus that targets bw + a projection layer (Ariadne / hypergraph), at design time enumerate which relationship classes bw's 0.13+ semantics will accept vs reject. Rejected classes persist in the manifest only and surface to the projection layer for ingest. Do NOT attempt to force the rejected relationships into bw via workaround (e.g., reverse-direction blocks).

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. Substrate doc-only edit; ~20-40 LOC extension to op-disc §16. Cross-reference the empirical anchor (ariadne--8fd.12 seeder run).

## Sequencing

P3. Substrate-canon refinement. Arc 25+ candidate. Not blocking anything — the factory-demo seeder already worked around the rejection by persisting in the manifest only; the substrate-prose update captures the discipline for future readers.

## Cross-references

- stoa--vmc — original bw-fit matrix ticket (closed Arc 23)
- Arc 23 op-disc §16 — current bw-fit matrix prose to extend
- ariadne--8fd.12 — empirical anchor; seeder run + close-out comment on the ticket has the bw-rejection log
- bw 0.13.0 release notes — the upstream rule definition
